title: Token-rate hedge and role-staggered hiring proposal
summary: Working sheet that tests a token-price hedging approach coupled with a role-stagger hiring cadence to smooth monthly burn under token-cost shocks. Includes three pricing sensitivity scenarios, headcount phasing, and quick heuristics for runway preservation.
high_level_objective: Preserve runway and SLAs by combining short-duration token price hedges with phased hiring (staggered offers and start dates) to avoid cliff increases in monthly GPU/token spend.
assumptions: Current blended token cost: $0.00012/token (hosted + dedicated mix)
Hiring lead time (offer->start): flexible window 4-10 weeks if staggered
Hedge vehicle can cap token cost for up to 3 months with 80% coverage at predictable premium
No immediate change in revenue; pricing elasticities modeled separately
SLA requirement: 99.9% uptime; capacity cannot drop below 85% baseline
quick_formulas_and_notes: monthly_hc_cost_usd = sum(new_FTEs * fully_burdened_cost) (phased hires pro-rated by month)
runway_delta_months approximated by dividing additional monthly burn into current cash cushion
Hedge premium modeled as ~10-20% extra over base token price but caps volatility for covered tokens
Staggered hiring implemented as 3-month ramp: month1 33%, month2 67%, month3 100% of target FTEs
Important: hedging instruments assumed to be non-dilutive to customer SLAs up to 90% coverage
detailed_notes: Rationale: token-cost shocks are the fastest lever to blow burn estimates when customers increase embed/generation volume or open models push per-token costs up. Traditional HC freezes shift load to infra and cause latency regressions; mixed approach reduces both risks.
Design of hedge: short-term swap-like instrument that purchases price protection on tokens consumed; modelled for 1-3 month tenors because forecasting beyond that is noisy.
Operational: implement 'hedge budget' as a separate line item in monthly run-rate and track utilization against actual token consumption via Console telemetry.

Hiring cadence: move from big-batch new hire starts to role-staggering allowing us to pause remaining starts if token costs spike mid-ramp. Legal/People OK with flexible start windows shared in initial offer letters.
Tradeoffs: hedging reduces volatility but has explicit premium; may be inefficient if prices fall. Staggered hiring increases administrative overhead and can extend time to value for product teams.

Contingency triggers: if token price > 2x base for two consecutive weeks, pause non-critical role starts and increase hedge coverage to 100% for next billing period (subject to available hedge capacity).
Sensitivity outputs here are intentionally coarse. Next step is to run Monte Carlo with sequence-length and customer-growth correlated shocks (request to Applied ML for traces).
recommendations: 1) Pilot a 2-month hedge covering 50% of forecasted token usage for Q2 to validate premium and operational hooking to invoicing.
2) Convert hiring reqs for next quarter into staggered start cohorts (apply to Eng infra, SRE, and Observability first).
3) Add a 'token-hedge' line to monthly finance pack; track realized vs. modeled savings weekly.
4) Build a simple dashboard in Console showing hedge coverage, token consumption vs forecast, and active start cohort status.
5) Re-run sensitivity with Applied ML request for real trace sampling and include revenue elasticity in next iteration.

conclusion: A small, time-boxed hedge plus a role-stagger hiring policy appears to materially reduce immediate runway risk from token-price shocks while preserving hiring flexibility. Recommend pilot and tighter telemetry before wider rollout.
